pre_existing_defect_disclosed.summary: tokenizer/tokenizer.json (already tracked on master, NOT part of this landing) fails to load directly via tokenizers.Tokenizer.from_str -- raises 'Exception: Token <literal> out of vocabulary' naming a five-letter merge-table literal not present in the vocab dict. Reproduced with a minimal isolated script that only reads the tracked tokenizer file and calls Tokenizer.from_str on its raw bytes (tokenizers==0.22.2 installed here), with zero involvement of any file in this PR. This is a defect in an already-tracked artifact / a tokenizers-library-version format mismatch, out of scope for a portability landing.
pre_existing_defect_disclosed.impact: ember_cbase_avir_data.py's and ember_cbase_avir_data_v2.py's _load_production_tokenizer() call (and therefore run_pipeline()) cannot complete on this defect. test_ember_cbase_avir_data.py: 0/4 tests reach completion (all 4 call run_pipeline() directly, each failing at the same tokenizer load line). test_ember_cbase_avir_data_v2.py: 98 of 99 sub-assertions PASS -- only test_full_pipeline_round_trip (the one test requiring the real tokenizer) fails on the identical exception. The other 98 sub-assertions exercise real pipeline logic (train/heldout firewall across all 44 tasks, answer-perturbation detection, gate assertions, tool-call counting) and all pass, which is strong evidence the imports and wiring in both modules and both test files are correct -- the failure isolates precisely to the pre-existing tokenizer artifact.
pre_existing_defect_disclosed.landed_anyway: Yes -- same precedent as #768 (family 3): byte-identical files with a disclosed downstream defect they did not introduce are landed, not held hostage to an unrelated fix. convert_nf4_prequant.py has zero tokenizer dependency (governor + torch only) and is fully functional.
